newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks erase losses, seen topping out.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks erase losses, seen topping out.

text.p: Argentine stocks recouped early losses and closed higher again Thursday but momentum could soon start to fizzle, dealers said.

"All expectations have been fulfilled, from International Monetary Fund approval of fiscal targets to congressional debate of tax bills," said Jorge Bonanno at brokers Interfin. "The inertia from recent gains could keep the market in positive territory Friday but it may soon run into stiff resistance."
The blue-chip MerVal index rose 0.8 percent to 552.04, stretching gains this week to 2.1 percent.
Analysts said next Tuesday's meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve loomed large in the markets.

"If the Fed raises rates and Wall Street slumps the bolsa will follow suit, because it has very little volume and thus no real strength," said Bonanno. "If bidding were to pick up the outlook would improve and the MerVal could aim for a near-term target of 570."

One factor contributing to the lack of volume is spreading talk of the possibility of a devaluation of the peso currency, which has been pegged at par with the dollar since April of 1991, traders said.

"It's not convenient or even necessary to devalue now, but just like inflation grabbed everyone's attention for years now the catchword is unemployment, which means that convertibility comes under scrutiny," said an analyst at a foreign-based emerging markets investment bank.

"From now on more and more people will join the devaluation debate, and although you can't have a fixed exchange rate forever the best argument against changing it now is that exports are extremely healthy," the analyst said.
The broad market rose 0.5 percent in the session, with winners beating losers 28 to 11 and 25 issues closing flat.
Floor volume was fractionally lower than Wednesday at 14.4 million pesos, while over-the-counter deals swelled to 81.5 million pesos from 60.4 million Wednesday.

The day's top main-tier performers were pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which surged 8.1 percent, steelmaker Siderca, which advanced 2.9 percent, and construction stock Polledo and foods giant Molinos, both up 2.2 percent.
The only MerVal loss was recorded by carmaker Ciadea, which shed 1.1 percent.
